correctness.rationale: Reconstruct the assigned regularized implicit equation F(q,ρ)=q cos(πρ)S0(qρ,(1+ρ)π)−πsinc(πρ)[1+qρC0(qρ,(1+ρ)π)]. At ρ=0, F(q,0)=qS−π with S=Si(π)>0, so q(0)=κ=π/S and F_q(κ,0)=S. The integral C0 has cos(at)−1=O(t²) and S0 has sin(at)=O(t), so logarithmic derivatives are absolutely integrable near t=0, justifying the implicit-function C² regularity. Independent derivative reconstruction gives F_ρ(κ,0)=κ²A−πκB, A=∫log t sin(πt)/t, B=∫(cosπt−1)/t. Therefore q′(0)=−F_ρ/F_q=κ²(SB−A)/S and ν=qρ=κρ+βρ²+O(ρ³). Independent high-precision quadrature gave β≈−0.6128110975066; solving the implicit equation at ρ=0.02,0.01,0.005 produced slopes approaching β. Numerical checks are supporting, not proof.
